newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Electrolux says Europe behind profit fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Electrolux says Europe behind profit fall.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux AB on Friday posted a 19 percent fall in profits for 1996 and, echoing U.S. rival Whirlpool, blamed a weaker European market.
Improved markets in North America and other parts of the, forecasting a strong U.S. market in the coming quarters.
"The markets are still sluggish in Germany, France and Italy, but you can expect an upturn," Chief executive Leif Johansson told a news conference.
"Our opinion is that (the U.S. market) feels strong in the coming quarters," he added.
Electrolux posted a profit of 3.25 billion crowns ($450.6 million) after financial items compared to 4.02 billion for 1995. Sales fell five percent to 110 billion crowns compared to a year earlier.
The company also announced long awaited plans to distribute shares in its wholly-owned unit, aluminium profile maker Granges, to Electrolux shareholders.
Electrolux shares fell sharply after the result but recovered later to 431 crowns, down two on the day.
The result fell short of market expectations, which had put the profit at 3.49 billion crowns after financial items.
"It was a mixed bag of news. For the core businesses it was a disappointment earnings-wise," one analyst said.

"On the positive side of course is that they have finally found a solution to the Granges problem. I think this shows they are more focussed on creating shareholder value now than in the past," said the Stockholm-based analyst.

Competitor Whirlpool Corp., the biggest maker of home appliances in the United States, on Tuesday reported a sharp rebound in earnings for the latest quarter, thanks to outstanding gains in North American and Latin American markets.
Like Whirlpool, Electrolux said group sales picked up in the fourth quarter, rising to 27.08 billion crowns from 26.98 billion and pinned gains to the U.S. market.
Electrolux also said a stronger Swedish crown had reduced competitiveness and cut its profit by 300 to 350 million crowns.
The 1996 result for Electrolux's largest household appliance unit was 2.46 billion crowns compared to 2.58 billion in 1995.

"The total U.S. market for whitegoods showed higher volume. Frigidaire Company reported a marked improvement in operating result on the basis of lower production costs and a better product mix," it said.
Operating income after depreciation for the fourth quarter fell 20 percent to 1.14 billion crowns because of restructuring and start-up costs.
Separately, Granges said its 1996 operating profit fell sharply to 461 million crowns compared with 831 in 1995.
Sales for Granges, Europe's second largest producer of extruded aluminium profiles and thin foil, totalled 10.01 billion crowns in 1996 compared to 11.45 a year earlier.

Electrolux announced in 1995 it would list Granges and said at the time its expected a one-off capital gain of around 1.5 billion crowns for the sale. Later it abandoned the plan because of negative developments on share markets.
Paul Hansson, analyst at Sweden's Nordbanken, said the move was expected in 1997 and the timing for the sale was better now than it was last time.

"There may be a bit more uncertainty about them succeeding this time with the sale, given the track record from last time because the timing was wrong," Hansson told Reuters. "But it's better to be too early in the business cycle than too late."
Electrolux said preliminary discussions with the Swedish tax board indicated Lex Asea regulations would be applicable in the Granges share sale, which will not include recycling operations.
